checkpoint: 1 — the pack's numbers re-measured with this task's own command, and the frame before the pack is connected
note: Second vertical subtask of Issue #77: connect the v2 creature pack. The branch is agent/77-goblin-pack-v2, based on agent/77-body-scale-170 (bb43700) and not on main, because it continues that subtask and goes to main paired with it. PNGs land under .artifacts/evidence/77-pack-before/ per Resolve-EvidenceOutputRoot and are not committed. Hashes and checksums are copied from the manifest capture-evidence.ps1 itself wrote (.artifacts/evidence/77-pack-before/manifest.json), not retyped.

entryCondition.claim: The base branch predates the pack it is supposed to connect, and that was found by measuring rather than by reading.
entryCondition.found: At bb43700 the flinch PNG measured alpha bbox (29, 24, 211, 188) — the pre-#165 flinch without the spear, which docs/art/goblin-v2-provenance.md lists as the struck-through row of its placement table. Issue #165 landed in main as 2b837c0 after agent/77-body-scale-170 was cut.
entryCondition.action: origin/main merged into this branch as the first commit of the task (merge 18afe51 of 2b837c0). The merge is clean — git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD returned a tree with no conflicts before it was taken — and it brings two commits: #165 (the flinch PNG only) and #171 (simulation: memory of place pays in time and need).
entryCondition.assetsUntouched: src/DungeonFortress.Game/assets/** is read-only for this task. The new flinch arrives as somebody else's merged commit; nothing here edits a PNG.
entryCondition.afterTheMerge: The same measurement returns (26, 24, 211, 188), which is the current row of the provenance table.

packMeasurement.claim: The numbers this task builds on are re-measured here rather than copied from the brief. They agree with docs/art/goblin-v2-provenance.md.
packMeasurement.command:
python -c "from PIL import Image; from pathlib import Path; base=Path('src/DungeonFortress.Game/assets/generated/goblins')
for s in ['idle','work','combat','windup','flinch','downed']:
    im=Image.open(base/f'goblin_{s}_v2.png').convert('RGBA'); a=im.getchannel('A'); px=a.load(); bbox=a.getbbox()
    xs=[x for y in range(172,188) for x in range(im.width) if px[x,y]>32]
    print(s, im.mode, im.width, im.height, bbox, bbox[3]-1, bbox[1], (min(xs)+max(xs))/2, bbox[3]-bbox[1])"
packMeasurement.commandNote: Method taken from the provenance document's own verification commands 1-4: alpha channel via Pillow, support zone 172 <= y <= 187, support centre over pixels with alpha > 32. Run from the root of this worktree with Python 3.12.10 and Pillow.
agreed: All six states are RGBA 272x192 — aspect ratio 272/192 = 17/12 exactly.
All six end on the same last opaque row y = 187, i.e. the exclusive alpha bound is 188 of 192 rows.
The support centre is 135.5 for four states and 136.0 for work and windup; the spread is 0.5 px on a 272 px canvas, which is the figure the provenance document states.
Every canvas edge column and row is fully transparent (verification command 5 of the provenance document, re-run here with the same result).

derivation.claim: The two numbers this subtask puts into the code follow from the canvas, and neither is typed in.

supportFraction.whyItMatters: GoblinFootLine is ReferenceGoblinDrawSize * WorldVisualScale * (SpriteSupportFraction - 0.5). Left at 92/96 with a 188/192 pack, the drawn feet land 20 * (40/22) * (188/192 - 92/96) = 0.3788 px below the ground at tile 40, and the whole sprite with them. Small, silent, and wrong on every creature at once.

canvasAspect.note: The brief quotes 87.55 px, which is the provenance document's rounding of the same quantity (61.8 * 17/12 = 87.55). The code carries the ratio, so the exact value is 87.575757575757578 and the difference is only how many digits 61.8 was quoted to.
canvasAspect.heightUnchanged: 61.81818181818182 px at tile 40 — GoblinDrawSize keeps its meaning as the canvas height, which is what the pack was authored against (docs/art/goblin-v2-provenance.md: «prepared for a 61.8 px canvas height»).
